_doc: Task 65 (scripts/systems/visit_door.gd): a visitor to the player's home walks to the front door and knocks; nobody walks in uninvited. walk_min = how long the walk up to the door may take; knock_again_min / give_up_min = when an unanswered visitor knocks again and leaves; doorstep_min = how long a talk on the doorstep lasts. Guests inside ask before the bathroom and keep out of the fridge and the beds (private_defs, cooldown_min after they are stopped). stay_refuse = the chance a guest asked to leave won't go (more for a hothead). Friendship changes: snub (ignored when you were clearly in), sent_away, argued, police.

knock: Somebody knocks at the front door.
knock_again: Another knock. Whoever it is isn't going away yet.
look: Through the window: {n}, waiting on the step.
You peek through the window. It's {n}.
why_visit: "Hi! I was passing and thought I'd say hello."
"Got a minute? I was in the area."
"Hello! Not a bad time, is it?"
"I baked too much. Thought you might want some."
"I couldn't face my own four walls tonight. Mind some company?"
"I've had the worst day. Got time for a cup of something?"
"I owed you a visit. Here I am."
gave_up: The knocking stops. Whoever it was has gone.
Footsteps go back down the path.
came_by: {n}: "Came by your place earlier. Guess you were out."
bath_ask: {n} hovers by the bathroom. "Mind if I use your bathroom?"
"Sorry, could I use your loo?" {n} asks.
{n} shifts from foot to foot. "Where's your bathroom?"
bath_no: {n} nods. "No problem." They look a little uncomfortable.
leave_ok: "Is that the time? I'll get going." {n} heads for the door.
"Right, I'll let you get some rest." {n} gets up to go.
leave_refuse: {n} doesn't move. "I've only just sat down."
insist: Words are said. {n} storms out and slams the door.
It turns into a row. {n} leaves angry.
police: You pick up the phone. {n} goes, muttering, before anyone comes.
